title: Justifying faith: knowledge, assent, trust; instrument
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Faith stands as ye organ or instrument belonging toward justification, not a meritorious cause; Christ and His righteousness stand as ye object and foundation. Faith apprehends; it does not earn. — In justifying faith concur knowledge belonging toward Gospel truth, firm assent, and ye trust by which ye sinner rests on Christ alone for remission belonging toward sins and acceptance with God.
pass_b_english: In justifying faith concur knowledge of Gospel truth, firm assent, and the trust by which the sinner rests on Christ alone for remission of sins and acceptance with God.
Faith is the organ or instrument of justification, not a meritorious cause; Christ and His righteousness are the object and foundation. Faith apprehends; it does not earn.
source_text: In fide iustificante concurrunt notitia veritatis Euangelicae, assensus firmus, et fiducia qua peccator in solum Christum pro remissione peccatorum et acceptatione apud Deum recumbit. Fides est organon sive instrumentum iustificationis, non causa meritoria; Christus et eius iustitia sunt obiectum et fundamentum. Fides apprehendit, non meretur.
